title: Scalar extraction and cocycle identity for matrix descent defects
statement: Let $K$ be a field, $S=K^{sep}$, and $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(S)$ with its Krull topology. Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional central simple $K$-algebra, $n>0$, and $e:S\otimes_K A\simeq M_n(S)$ an $S$-algebra equivalence. Suppose $b:G\to GL_n(S)$ is locally constant and $g(e(1\otimes a))=b_g^{-1}e(1\otimes a)b_g$ for every $g\in G$ and $a\in A$. Then there exists a jointly locally constant $c:G\times G\to S^\times$ satisfying $b_g g(b_h)=c(g,h)b_{gh}$ and $c(g,h)c(gh,k)=g(c(h,k))c(g,hk)$ for all $g,h,k$. Scalar matrices are as in [def-sc-brauer-scalar-defect], and the Galois action is as in [def-sc-galois-units-cohomology].

proof.text: Form D(g,h) = b(g) map(g,b(h)) b(gh)⁻¹. Applying g to the descent equation for h and then using that for g gives equal conjugations by b(g) map(g,b(h)) and b(gh). Multiplication by the inverse units proves that D commutes with e(1 ⊗ a). TensorProduct.induction_on and scalar linearity extend this to all tensors; surjectivity of e makes D central in GL_n(S). Mathlib Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.center_eq_range_scalar supplies its scalar unit. Evaluation at the (0,0) entry proves scalar injectivity because n ≠ 0, so the unit is unique.

Give S the discrete topology locally in the proof. Mathlib stabilizer_isOpen_of_isIntegral and continuousSMul_iff_stabilizer_isOpen imply that g ↦ g(x) is locally constant. Two finite LocallyConstant.unflip operations establish this entrywise for a fixed matrix, and Units.val_injective transports it to GL_n(S). On a neighborhood of (g,h), first fix b(h) using hb; then fix the action of g on this fixed matrix. Products, inversion and continuous group multiplication prove local constancy of D. IsLocallyConstant.desc and scalar injectivity transfer it to the chosen c.

Expand b(g) map(g,b(h)) map(gh,b(k)) using the scalar relation in both associative orders. Use map_mul, map_scalar, and scalar_commute; cancel b(ghk), then use scalar injectivity. Applying Units.val yields exactly the stated scalar cocycle identity.
